- **Basic search** (`basic`) costs **1 API credit per request**.
- **Advanced search** (`advanced`) costs **2 API credits per request**.
These credits are deducted from your monthly allowance or pay‑as‑you‑go balance. The pricing overview also notes that free users receive 1,000 credits each month, with pay‑as‑you‑go credits priced at $0.008 each and monthly plans offering lower per‑credit rates【78dc8eaa-ba26-47a5-97d1-057e48d122c8】. The changelog confirms the same credit costs for the two search depths【58860a3c-d336-45f9-a24f-3f37b29c260a】.

```
* **`search_depth`** (`basic` or `advanced`, default `basic`): `advanced` retrieves the most relevant sources and content snippets for your query, while `basic` returns generic snippets from each source. `basic` costs 1 API credit; `advanced` costs 2.
* **`chunks_per_source`**: the maximum number of relevant chunks (short snippets up to 500 characters each) returned per source, which controls content length. Chunks appear in the `content` field as  `[...]  [...]` . Available only when `search_depth` is `advanced`. Range: 1 to 3.

* `include_answer`, `include_raw_content`, and `max_results` must always be set manually, since they affect response size.
* `search_depth` may be set to `advanced` automatically when that’s likely to improve results, which costs **2 API credits per request**. Set `search_depth` to `basic` explicitly to avoid the extra cost.

* **Basic search now returns chunks.** `basic` previously returned a single page summary per source. It now returns multiple semantically relevant snippets per URL, so `results[].content` may contain several chunks joined by `[...]`.
* **`chunks_per_source` now applies to `basic`.** It previously affected `advanced` and `fast`, and now controls the number of chunks per source at those depths plus `basic`.
* **Choosing between depths.** `advanced` still offers broader coverage and the highest relevance at higher latency. See [basic vs advanced](/documentation/best-practices/best-practices-search#basic-vs-advanced).
```

`getUserMedia()` ist ein starkes Merkmal, das nur in [sicheren Kontexten](/de/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts) verwendet werden kann; in unsicheren Kontexten ist `navigator.mediaDevices` `undefined`, was den Zugriff auf `getUserMedia()` verhindert. Ein sicherer Kontext ist kurz gesagt, eine Seite, die mit HTTPS oder dem `file:///` URL-Schema geladen wird, oder eine Seite von `localhost`.

Die `getUserMedia()`-Methode ist nur in [sicheren Kontexten](/de/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts) verfügbar. Ein sicherer Kontext ist einer, in dem der Browser mit hinlänglichem Vertrauen annimmt, dass das Dokument sicher geladen wurde, mit HTTPS/TLS, und beschränkten Kontakt zu unsicheren Kontexten hat. Wenn ein Dokument nicht in einem sicheren Kontext geladen wird, ist die [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/de/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) Eigenschaft `undefined`, was den Zugang zu `getUserMedia()` unmöglich macht.

`NotAllowedError` [`DOMException`](/de/docs/Web/API/DOMException)
:   Ausgelöst, wenn eines oder mehrere der angeforderten Quellgeräte derzeit nicht verwendet werden können. Dies tritt auf, wenn der Browsing-Kontext unsicher ist (d.h. die Seite wurde mit HTTP anstelle von HTTPS geladen). Es tritt auch auf, wenn der Benutzer angegeben hat, dass die aktuelle Browsing-Instanz keinen Zugriff auf das Gerät erhält, der Benutzer den Zugriff für die aktuelle Sitzung verweigert hat oder der Benutzer den Zugriff auf Benutzer-Mediengeräte weltweit verweigert hat. In Browsern, die die Verwaltung von Medienberechtigungen mit [Permissions Policy](/de/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/Permissions_Policy) unterstützen, wird dieser Fehler zurückgegeben, wenn die Permissions Policy nicht so konfiguriert ist, dass sie den Zugriff auf die Eingabequelle(n) erlaubt.

[`TypeError`](/de/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypeError)
:   Ausgelöst, wenn die Liste der angegebenen Einschränkungen leer ist oder alle Einschränkungen auf `false` gesetzt sind. Dies kann auch passieren, wenn Sie versuchen, `getUserMedia()` in einem unsicheren Kontext aufzurufen, da [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/de/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) in einem unsicheren Kontext `undefined` ist.

Aufgrund des offensichtlichen Sicherheitsanliegens, das mit `getUserMedia()` in unerwarteten Situationen oder ohne sorgfältig gemanagte Sicherheit verbunden ist, kann es nur in sicheren Kontexten verwendet werden. Es gibt eine Anzahl unsicherer Wege, ein Dokument zu laden, das möglicherweise versuchen könnte, `getUserMedia()` aufzurufen. Die folgenden Beispiele zeigen Situationen, in denen `getUserMedia()` nicht aufgerufen werden darf:

`SecurityError` [`DOMException`](/de/docs/Web/API/DOMException)
:   Ausgelöst, wenn die Unterstützung von Benutzer-Medien im [`Document`](/de/docs/Web/API/Document) deaktiviert ist, auf dem `getUserMedia()` aufgerufen wurde. Der Mechanismus, durch den die Unterstützung für Benutzer-Medien aktiviert und deaktiviert wird, bleibt dem einzelnen Benutzeragenten überlassen.

Zusätzlich ist immer die Erlaubnis des Benutzers erforderlich, um auf die Audio- und Videoeingänge des Benutzers zuzugreifen. Nur das Top-Level-Dokumentfenster eines gültigen Ursprungs kann die Erlaubnis zur Nutzung von `getUserMedia()` anfordern, es sei denn, der Top-Level-Kontext gewährt ausdrücklich einem bestimmten

Die **`getUserMedia()`**-Methode der [`MediaDevices`](/de/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices)-Schnittstelle fordert den Benutzer um Erlaubnis zur Nutzung eines Medieneingangs auf, welcher einen [`MediaStream`](/de/docs/Web/API/MediaStream) mit Spuren der angeforderten Medientypen erzeugt.

**Sicherer Kontext:** Diese Funktion ist nur in [sicheren Kontexten](/de/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts) (HTTPS) in einigen oder allen [unterstützenden Browsern](#browser-kompatibilität) verfügbar.

Als eine API, die signifikante Datenschutzbedenken hervorrufen kann, legt die Spezifikation von `getUserMedia()` eine Vielzahl von Datenschutz- und Sicherheitsanforderungen fest, die Browser erfüllen müssen.

Der Versuch, in dieser Situation auf `getUserMedia()` zuzugreifen, führt zu einem [`TypeError`](/de/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypeError).

sources.title: Firefox 68 release notes for developers - Mozilla | MDN
sources.content:
Secure contexts are those loaded using HTTPS, those located using the `file:///` scheme, and those loaded from `localhost`.

* [`getUserMedia()`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia "getUserMedia()") may no longer be used from a non-secure context; attempting to do so now throws a `NotAllowedError` exception.

* Disabled the feature to force unloading background tabs on low memory conditions, to prevent top-level browser contexts from magically disappearing ([Firefox bug 1553748](https://bugzil.la/1553748 "External link (opens in new tab)")).
* Disabled privileged content processes that caused HTTP authentication dialogs not to appear when navigating to a website after opening a new tab ([Firefox bug 1558763](https://bugzil.la/1558763 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

  **Note:** In the future, Firefox will also remove the [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) property on insecure contexts, preventing all access to the [`MediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices) APIs. **This is already the case in Nightly builds.**

For now, if you must, you can re-enable the ability to perform insecure calls to `getUserMedia()` by setting the preference `media.getusermedia.insecure.enabled` to `true` ([Firefox bug 1335740](https://bugzil.la/1335740 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

* The Web Audio API [`MediaStreamTrackAudioSourceNode`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaStreamTrackAudioSourceNode) interface is now supported, as is the method [`AudioContext.createMediaStreamTrackSource()`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/AudioContext/createMediaStreamTrackSource) ([Firefox bug 1324548](https://bugzil.la/1324548 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

* `proxyAuthorization` and `connectionIsolation` in [`proxy.onRequest`](/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/proxy/onRequest) now apply only to HTTPS proxies ([Firefox bug 1549368](https://bugzil.la/1549368 "External link (opens in new tab)").

* [`XMLHttpRequest`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/XMLHttpRequest) has been updated to no longer accept the non-standard `moz-chunked-arraybuffer` value for [`responseType`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/XMLHttpRequest/responseType "responseType").

* A `string` value, `cookieStoreId`, representing the cookie store ID of the current context, has been added to the [proxy.RequestDetails](/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/proxy/RequestDetails).

### [HTTP](#http)

* The [HTTP](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP) [`Clear-Site-Data`](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Clear-Site-Data) header no longer supports the `executionContexts` directive. This was removed due to problems with interactions between interconnections among different kinds of data at different points in the navigation process and the way the specification is designed. It [has been proposed](https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-clear-site-data/issues/59 "External link (opens in new tab)") that this directive be removed from the specification for this reason, among others ([Firefox bug 1548034](https://bugzil.la/1548034 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

* `XMLHttpRequest` now outputs a warning to console if you perform a synchronous request while handling an [`unload`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/unload_event "unload"), [`beforeunload`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/beforeunload_event "beforeunload"), or [`pagehide`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/pagehide_event "pagehide") event ([Firefox bug 980902](https://bugzil.la/980902 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

* The Network monitor [request list](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/devtools-user/network_monitor/request_list/index.html#filtering-requests "External link (opens in new tab)") now allows you to block a specific URL ([Firefox bug 1151368](https://bugzil.la/1151368 "External link (opens in new tab)")).
* You can now resend a network request without editing the method, URL, parameters, and headers, using the [Resend](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/devtools-user/network_monitor/request_list/index.html#context-menu "External link (opens in new tab)") command on the context menu ([Firefox bug 1422014](https://bugzil.la/1422014 "External link (opens in new tab)")).
* The context menu of the Network monitor [Headers](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/devtools-user/network_monitor/request_details/index.html#headers "External link (opens in new tab)") tab now allows you to copy all or some of the header information to the clipboard in JSON format ([Firefox bug 1442249](https://bugzil.la/1442249 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

sources.content:
`getUserMedia()` is a powerful feature that can only be used in [secure contexts](/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts); in insecure contexts, `navigator.mediaDevices` is `undefined`, preventing access to `getUserMedia()`. A secure context is, in short, a page loaded using HTTPS or the `file:///` URL scheme, or a page loaded from `localhost`.

The `getUserMedia()` method is only available in [secure contexts](/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts). A secure context is one the browser is reasonably confident contains a document which was loaded securely, using HTTPS/TLS, and has limited exposure to insecure contexts. If a document isn't loaded in a secure context, the [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) property is `undefined`, making access to `getUserMedia()` impossible.

`NotAllowedError` [`DOMException`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/DOMException)
:   Thrown if one or more of the requested source devices cannot be used at this time. This will happen if the browsing context is insecure (that is, the page was loaded using HTTP rather than HTTPS). It also happens if the user has specified that the current browsing instance is not permitted access to the device, the user has denied access for the current session, or the user has denied all access to user media devices globally. On browsers that support managing media permissions with [Permissions Policy](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/Permissions_Policy), this error is returned if Permissions Policy is not configured to allow access to the input source(s).

Because of the obvious security concern associated with `getUserMedia()` if used unexpectedly or without security being carefully managed, it can only be used in secure contexts. There are a number of insecure ways to load a document that might, in turn, attempt to call `getUserMedia()`. The following are examples of situations in which `getUserMedia()` is not permitted to be called:

[`TypeError`](/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypeError)
:   Thrown if the list of constraints specified is empty, or has all constraints set to `false`. This can also happen if you try to call `getUserMedia()` in an insecure context, since [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) is `undefined` in an insecure context.

**Secure context:** This feature is available only in [secure contexts](/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts) (HTTPS), in some or all [supporting browsers](#browser_compatibility).

In addition, user permission is always required to access the user's audio and video inputs. Only a window's top-level document context for a valid origin can even request permission to use `getUserMedia()`, unless the top-level context expressly grants permission for a given

`SecurityError` [`DOMException`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/DOMException)
:   Thrown if user media support is disabled on the [`Document`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document) on which `getUserMedia()` was called. The mechanism by which user media support is enabled and disabled is left up to the individual user agent.

The **`getUserMedia()`** method of the [`MediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices) interface prompts the user for permission to use a media input which produces a [`MediaStream`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaStream) with tracks containing the requested types of media.

As an API that may involve significant privacy concerns, `getUserMedia()`'s specification lays out a wide array of privacy and security requirements that browsers are obligated to meet.

Attempting to access `getUserMedia()` in this situation will result in a [`TypeError`](/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypeError).

# MediaDevices: getUserMedia() method

1. [Web](/en-US/docs/Web)
2. [Web APIs](/en-US/docs/Web/API)
3. [MediaDevices](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices)
4. [getUserMedia()](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia)

```
getUserMedia(constraints) 
```

```
* **`search_depth`** (`basic` or `advanced`, default `basic`): `advanced` retrieves the most relevant sources and content snippets for your query, while `basic` returns generic snippets from each source. `basic` costs 1 API credit; `advanced` costs 2.
* **`chunks_per_source`**: the maximum number of relevant chunks (short snippets up to 500 characters each) returned per source, which controls content length. Chunks appear in the `content` field as  `[...]  [...]` . Available only when `search_depth` is `advanced`. Range: 1 to 3.

* `include_answer`, `include_raw_content`, and `max_results` must always be set manually, since they affect response size.
* `search_depth` may be set to `advanced` automatically when that’s likely to improve results, which costs **2 API credits per request**. Set `search_depth` to `basic` explicitly to avoid the extra cost.

* **Basic search now returns chunks.** `basic` previously returned a single page summary per source. It now returns multiple semantically relevant snippets per URL, so `results[].content` may contain several chunks joined by `[...]`.
* **`chunks_per_source` now applies to `basic`.** It previously affected `advanced` and `fast`, and now controls the number of chunks per source at those depths plus `basic`.
* **Choosing between depths.** `advanced` still offers broader coverage and the highest relevance at higher latency. See [basic vs advanced](/documentation/best-practices/best-practices-search#basic-vs-advanced).

`getUserMedia()` ist ein starkes Merkmal, das nur in [sicheren Kontexten](/de/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts) verwendet werden kann; in unsicheren Kontexten ist `navigator.mediaDevices` `undefined`, was den Zugriff auf `getUserMedia()` verhindert. Ein sicherer Kontext ist kurz gesagt, eine Seite, die mit HTTPS oder dem `file:///` URL-Schema geladen wird, oder eine Seite von `localhost`.

Die `getUserMedia()`-Methode ist nur in [sicheren Kontexten](/de/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts) verfügbar. Ein sicherer Kontext ist einer, in dem der Browser mit hinlänglichem Vertrauen annimmt, dass das Dokument sicher geladen wurde, mit HTTPS/TLS, und beschränkten Kontakt zu unsicheren Kontexten hat. Wenn ein Dokument nicht in einem sicheren Kontext geladen wird, ist die [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/de/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) Eigenschaft `undefined`, was den Zugang zu `getUserMedia()` unmöglich macht.

`NotAllowedError` [`DOMException`](/de/docs/Web/API/DOMException)
:   Ausgelöst, wenn eines oder mehrere der angeforderten Quellgeräte derzeit nicht verwendet werden können. Dies tritt auf, wenn der Browsing-Kontext unsicher ist (d.h. die Seite wurde mit HTTP anstelle von HTTPS geladen). Es tritt auch auf, wenn der Benutzer angegeben hat, dass die aktuelle Browsing-Instanz keinen Zugriff auf das Gerät erhält, der Benutzer den Zugriff für die aktuelle Sitzung verweigert hat oder der Benutzer den Zugriff auf Benutzer-Mediengeräte weltweit verweigert hat. In Browsern, die die Verwaltung von Medienberechtigungen mit [Permissions Policy](/de/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/Permissions_Policy) unterstützen, wird dieser Fehler zurückgegeben, wenn die Permissions Policy nicht so konfiguriert ist, dass sie den Zugriff auf die Eingabequelle(n) erlaubt.

[`TypeError`](/de/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypeError)
:   Ausgelöst, wenn die Liste der angegebenen Einschränkungen leer ist oder alle Einschränkungen auf `false` gesetzt sind. Dies kann auch passieren, wenn Sie versuchen, `getUserMedia()` in einem unsicheren Kontext aufzurufen, da [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/de/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) in einem unsicheren Kontext `undefined` ist.

Aufgrund des offensichtlichen Sicherheitsanliegens, das mit `getUserMedia()` in unerwarteten Situationen oder ohne sorgfältig gemanagte Sicherheit verbunden ist, kann es nur in sicheren Kontexten verwendet werden. Es gibt eine Anzahl unsicherer Wege, ein Dokument zu laden, das möglicherweise versuchen könnte, `getUserMedia()` aufzurufen. Die folgenden Beispiele zeigen Situationen, in denen `getUserMedia()` nicht aufgerufen werden darf:

`SecurityError` [`DOMException`](/de/docs/Web/API/DOMException)
:   Ausgelöst, wenn die Unterstützung von Benutzer-Medien im [`Document`](/de/docs/Web/API/Document) deaktiviert ist, auf dem `getUserMedia()` aufgerufen wurde. Der Mechanismus, durch den die Unterstützung für Benutzer-Medien aktiviert und deaktiviert wird, bleibt dem einzelnen Benutzeragenten überlassen.

Zusätzlich ist immer die Erlaubnis des Benutzers erforderlich, um auf die Audio- und Videoeingänge des Benutzers zuzugreifen. Nur das Top-Level-Dokumentfenster eines gültigen Ursprungs kann die Erlaubnis zur Nutzung von `getUserMedia()` anfordern, es sei denn, der Top-Level-Kontext gewährt ausdrücklich einem bestimmten

Die **`getUserMedia()`**-Methode der [`MediaDevices`](/de/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices)-Schnittstelle fordert den Benutzer um Erlaubnis zur Nutzung eines Medieneingangs auf, welcher einen [`MediaStream`](/de/docs/Web/API/MediaStream) mit Spuren der angeforderten Medientypen erzeugt.

**Sicherer Kontext:** Diese Funktion ist nur in [sicheren Kontexten](/de/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts) (HTTPS) in einigen oder allen [unterstützenden Browsern](#browser-kompatibilität) verfügbar.

Als eine API, die signifikante Datenschutzbedenken hervorrufen kann, legt die Spezifikation von `getUserMedia()` eine Vielzahl von Datenschutz- und Sicherheitsanforderungen fest, die Browser erfüllen müssen.

Der Versuch, in dieser Situation auf `getUserMedia()` zuzugreifen, führt zu einem [`TypeError`](/de/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypeError).
```

```
sources.title: Firefox 68 release notes for developers - Mozilla | MDN
sources.content:
Secure contexts are those loaded using HTTPS, those located using the `file:///` scheme, and those loaded from `localhost`.

* [`getUserMedia()`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia "getUserMedia()") may no longer be used from a non-secure context; attempting to do so now throws a `NotAllowedError` exception.

* Disabled the feature to force unloading background tabs on low memory conditions, to prevent top-level browser contexts from magically disappearing ([Firefox bug 1553748](https://bugzil.la/1553748 "External link (opens in new tab)")).
* Disabled privileged content processes that caused HTTP authentication dialogs not to appear when navigating to a website after opening a new tab ([Firefox bug 1558763](https://bugzil.la/1558763 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

  **Note:** In the future, Firefox will also remove the [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) property on insecure contexts, preventing all access to the [`MediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices) APIs. **This is already the case in Nightly builds.**

For now, if you must, you can re-enable the ability to perform insecure calls to `getUserMedia()` by setting the preference `media.getusermedia.insecure.enabled` to `true` ([Firefox bug 1335740](https://bugzil.la/1335740 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

* The Web Audio API [`MediaStreamTrackAudioSourceNode`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaStreamTrackAudioSourceNode) interface is now supported, as is the method [`AudioContext.createMediaStreamTrackSource()`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/AudioContext/createMediaStreamTrackSource) ([Firefox bug 1324548](https://bugzil.la/1324548 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

* `proxyAuthorization` and `connectionIsolation` in [`proxy.onRequest`](/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/proxy/onRequest) now apply only to HTTPS proxies ([Firefox bug 1549368](https://bugzil.la/1549368 "External link (opens in new tab)").

* [`XMLHttpRequest`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/XMLHttpRequest) has been updated to no longer accept the non-standard `moz-chunked-arraybuffer` value for [`responseType`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/XMLHttpRequest/responseType "responseType").

* A `string` value, `cookieStoreId`, representing the cookie store ID of the current context, has been added to the [proxy.RequestDetails](/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/proxy/RequestDetails).

### [HTTP](#http)

* The [HTTP](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP) [`Clear-Site-Data`](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Clear-Site-Data) header no longer supports the `executionContexts` directive. This was removed due to problems with interactions between interconnections among different kinds of data at different points in the navigation process and the way the specification is designed. It [has been proposed](https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-clear-site-data/issues/59 "External link (opens in new tab)") that this directive be removed from the specification for this reason, among others ([Firefox bug 1548034](https://bugzil.la/1548034 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

* `XMLHttpRequest` now outputs a warning to console if you perform a synchronous request while handling an [`unload`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/unload_event "unload"), [`beforeunload`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/beforeunload_event "beforeunload"), or [`pagehide`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/pagehide_event "pagehide") event ([Firefox bug 980902](https://bugzil.la/980902 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

* The Network monitor [request list](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/devtools-user/network_monitor/request_list/index.html#filtering-requests "External link (opens in new tab)") now allows you to block a specific URL ([Firefox bug 1151368](https://bugzil.la/1151368 "External link (opens in new tab)")).
* You can now resend a network request without editing the method, URL, parameters, and headers, using the [Resend](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/devtools-user/network_monitor/request_list/index.html#context-menu "External link (opens in new tab)") command on the context menu ([Firefox bug 1422014](https://bugzil.la/1422014 "External link (opens in new tab)")).
* The context menu of the Network monitor [Headers](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/devtools-user/network_monitor/request_details/index.html#headers "External link (opens in new tab)") tab now allows you to copy all or some of the header information to the clipboard in JSON format ([Firefox bug 1442249](https://bugzil.la/1442249 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

sources.content:
`getUserMedia()` is a powerful feature that can only be used in [secure contexts](/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts); in insecure contexts, `navigator.mediaDevices` is `undefined`, preventing access to `getUserMedia()`. A secure context is, in short, a page loaded using HTTPS or the `file:///` URL scheme, or a page loaded from `localhost`.

The `getUserMedia()` method is only available in [secure contexts](/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts). A secure context is one the browser is reasonably confident contains a document which was loaded securely, using HTTPS/TLS, and has limited exposure to insecure contexts. If a document isn't loaded in a secure context, the [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) property is `undefined`, making access to `getUserMedia()` impossible.

`NotAllowedError` [`DOMException`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/DOMException)
:   Thrown if one or more of the requested source devices cannot be used at this time. This will happen if the browsing context is insecure (that is, the page was loaded using HTTP rather than HTTPS). It also happens if the user has specified that the current browsing instance is not permitted access to the device, the user has denied access for the current session, or the user has denied all access to user media devices globally. On browsers that support managing media permissions with [Permissions Policy](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/Permissions_Policy), this error is returned if Permissions Policy is not configured to allow access to the input source(s).

Because of the obvious security concern associated with `getUserMedia()` if used unexpectedly or without security being carefully managed, it can only be used in secure contexts. There are a number of insecure ways to load a document that might, in turn, attempt to call `getUserMedia()`. The following are examples of situations in which `getUserMedia()` is not permitted to be called:

[`TypeError`](/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypeError)
:   Thrown if the list of constraints specified is empty, or has all constraints set to `false`. This can also happen if you try to call `getUserMedia()` in an insecure context, since [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) is `undefined` in an insecure context.

**Secure context:** This feature is available only in [secure contexts](/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts) (HTTPS), in some or all [supporting browsers](#browser_compatibility).

In addition, user permission is always required to access the user's audio and video inputs. Only a window's top-level document context for a valid origin can even request permission to use `getUserMedia()`, unless the top-level context expressly grants permission for a given

`SecurityError` [`DOMException`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/DOMException)
:   Thrown if user media support is disabled on the [`Document`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document) on which `getUserMedia()` was called. The mechanism by which user media support is enabled and disabled is left up to the individual user agent.

The **`getUserMedia()`** method of the [`MediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices) interface prompts the user for permission to use a media input which produces a [`MediaStream`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaStream) with tracks containing the requested types of media.

As an API that may involve significant privacy concerns, `getUserMedia()`'s specification lays out a wide array of privacy and security requirements that browsers are obligated to meet.

Attempting to access `getUserMedia()` in this situation will result in a [`TypeError`](/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypeError).

# MediaDevices: getUserMedia() method

1. [Web](/en-US/docs/Web)
2. [Web APIs](/en-US/docs/Web/API)
3. [MediaDevices](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices)
4. [getUserMedia()](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia)

```
getUserMedia(constraints) 

* **`search_depth`** (`basic` or `advanced`, default `basic`): `advanced` retrieves the most relevant sources and content snippets for your query, while `basic` returns generic snippets from each source. `basic` costs 1 API credit; `advanced` costs 2.
* **`chunks_per_source`**: the maximum number of relevant chunks (short snippets up to 500 characters each) returned per source, which controls content length. Chunks appear in the `content` field as  `[...]  [...]` . Available only when `search_depth` is `advanced`. Range: 1 to 3.

* `include_answer`, `include_raw_content`, and `max_results` must always be set manually, since they affect response size.
* `search_depth` may be set to `advanced` automatically when that’s likely to improve results, which costs **2 API credits per request**. Set `search_depth` to `basic` explicitly to avoid the extra cost.

* **Basic search now returns chunks.** `basic` previously returned a single page summary per source. It now returns multiple semantically relevant snippets per URL, so `results[].content` may contain several chunks joined by `[...]`.
* **`chunks_per_source` now applies to `basic`.** It previously affected `advanced` and `fast`, and now controls the number of chunks per source at those depths plus `basic`.
* **Choosing between depths.** `advanced` still offers broader coverage and the highest relevance at higher latency. See [basic vs advanced](/documentation/best-practices/best-practices-search#basic-vs-advanced).

In an insecure context the `navigator.mediaDevices` property is undefined, making access to the microphone impossible. [7b6b5044-a494-4284-83bc-181eeb0920bf][8d95c57b-7c94-4396-b2b4-9e7cbb142b72]

sources.content:
`getUserMedia()` ist ein starkes Merkmal, das nur in [sicheren Kontexten](/de/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts) verwendet werden kann; in unsicheren Kontexten ist `navigator.mediaDevices` `undefined`, was den Zugriff auf `getUserMedia()` verhindert. Ein sicherer Kontext ist kurz gesagt, eine Seite, die mit HTTPS oder dem `file:///` URL-Schema geladen wird, oder eine Seite von `localhost`.

Die `getUserMedia()`-Methode ist nur in [sicheren Kontexten](/de/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts) verfügbar. Ein sicherer Kontext ist einer, in dem der Browser mit hinlänglichem Vertrauen annimmt, dass das Dokument sicher geladen wurde, mit HTTPS/TLS, und beschränkten Kontakt zu unsicheren Kontexten hat. Wenn ein Dokument nicht in einem sicheren Kontext geladen wird, ist die [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/de/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) Eigenschaft `undefined`, was den Zugang zu `getUserMedia()` unmöglich macht.

`NotAllowedError` [`DOMException`](/de/docs/Web/API/DOMException)
:   Ausgelöst, wenn eines oder mehrere der angeforderten Quellgeräte derzeit nicht verwendet werden können. Dies tritt auf, wenn der Browsing-Kontext unsicher ist (d.h. die Seite wurde mit HTTP anstelle von HTTPS geladen). Es tritt auch auf, wenn der Benutzer angegeben hat, dass die aktuelle Browsing-Instanz keinen Zugriff auf das Gerät erhält, der Benutzer den Zugriff für die aktuelle Sitzung verweigert hat oder der Benutzer den Zugriff auf Benutzer-Mediengeräte weltweit verweigert hat. In Browsern, die die Verwaltung von Medienberechtigungen mit [Permissions Policy](/de/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/Permissions_Policy) unterstützen, wird dieser Fehler zurückgegeben, wenn die Permissions Policy nicht so konfiguriert ist, dass sie den Zugriff auf die Eingabequelle(n) erlaubt.

[`TypeError`](/de/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypeError)
:   Ausgelöst, wenn die Liste der angegebenen Einschränkungen leer ist oder alle Einschränkungen auf `false` gesetzt sind. Dies kann auch passieren, wenn Sie versuchen, `getUserMedia()` in einem unsicheren Kontext aufzurufen, da [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/de/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) in einem unsicheren Kontext `undefined` ist.

Aufgrund des offensichtlichen Sicherheitsanliegens, das mit `getUserMedia()` in unerwarteten Situationen oder ohne sorgfältig gemanagte Sicherheit verbunden ist, kann es nur in sicheren Kontexten verwendet werden. Es gibt eine Anzahl unsicherer Wege, ein Dokument zu laden, das möglicherweise versuchen könnte, `getUserMedia()` aufzurufen. Die folgenden Beispiele zeigen Situationen, in denen `getUserMedia()` nicht aufgerufen werden darf:

`SecurityError` [`DOMException`](/de/docs/Web/API/DOMException)
:   Ausgelöst, wenn die Unterstützung von Benutzer-Medien im [`Document`](/de/docs/Web/API/Document) deaktiviert ist, auf dem `getUserMedia()` aufgerufen wurde. Der Mechanismus, durch den die Unterstützung für Benutzer-Medien aktiviert und deaktiviert wird, bleibt dem einzelnen Benutzeragenten überlassen.

Zusätzlich ist immer die Erlaubnis des Benutzers erforderlich, um auf die Audio- und Videoeingänge des Benutzers zuzugreifen. Nur das Top-Level-Dokumentfenster eines gültigen Ursprungs kann die Erlaubnis zur Nutzung von `getUserMedia()` anfordern, es sei denn, der Top-Level-Kontext gewährt ausdrücklich einem bestimmten

Die **`getUserMedia()`**-Methode der [`MediaDevices`](/de/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices)-Schnittstelle fordert den Benutzer um Erlaubnis zur Nutzung eines Medieneingangs auf, welcher einen [`MediaStream`](/de/docs/Web/API/MediaStream) mit Spuren der angeforderten Medientypen erzeugt.

**Sicherer Kontext:** Diese Funktion ist nur in [sicheren Kontexten](/de/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts) (HTTPS) in einigen oder allen [unterstützenden Browsern](#browser-kompatibilität) verfügbar.

Als eine API, die signifikante Datenschutzbedenken hervorrufen kann, legt die Spezifikation von `getUserMedia()` eine Vielzahl von Datenschutz- und Sicherheitsanforderungen fest, die Browser erfüllen müssen.

Der Versuch, in dieser Situation auf `getUserMedia()` zuzugreifen, führt zu einem [`TypeError`](/de/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypeError).

sources.title: Firefox 68 release notes for developers - Mozilla | MDN
sources.content:
Secure contexts are those loaded using HTTPS, those located using the `file:///` scheme, and those loaded from `localhost`.

* [`getUserMedia()`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia "getUserMedia()") may no longer be used from a non-secure context; attempting to do so now throws a `NotAllowedError` exception.

* Disabled the feature to force unloading background tabs on low memory conditions, to prevent top-level browser contexts from magically disappearing ([Firefox bug 1553748](https://bugzil.la/1553748 "External link (opens in new tab)")).
* Disabled privileged content processes that caused HTTP authentication dialogs not to appear when navigating to a website after opening a new tab ([Firefox bug 1558763](https://bugzil.la/1558763 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

  **Note:** In the future, Firefox will also remove the [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) property on insecure contexts, preventing all access to the [`MediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices) APIs. **This is already the case in Nightly builds.**

For now, if you must, you can re-enable the ability to perform insecure calls to `getUserMedia()` by setting the preference `media.getusermedia.insecure.enabled` to `true` ([Firefox bug 1335740](https://bugzil.la/1335740 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

* The Web Audio API [`MediaStreamTrackAudioSourceNode`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaStreamTrackAudioSourceNode) interface is now supported, as is the method [`AudioContext.createMediaStreamTrackSource()`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/AudioContext/createMediaStreamTrackSource) ([Firefox bug 1324548](https://bugzil.la/1324548 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

* `proxyAuthorization` and `connectionIsolation` in [`proxy.onRequest`](/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/proxy/onRequest) now apply only to HTTPS proxies ([Firefox bug 1549368](https://bugzil.la/1549368 "External link (opens in new tab)").

* [`XMLHttpRequest`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/XMLHttpRequest) has been updated to no longer accept the non-standard `moz-chunked-arraybuffer` value for [`responseType`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/XMLHttpRequest/responseType "responseType").

* A `string` value, `cookieStoreId`, representing the cookie store ID of the current context, has been added to the [proxy.RequestDetails](/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/proxy/RequestDetails).

### [HTTP](#http)

* The [HTTP](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP) [`Clear-Site-Data`](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Clear-Site-Data) header no longer supports the `executionContexts` directive. This was removed due to problems with interactions between interconnections among different kinds of data at different points in the navigation process and the way the specification is designed. It [has been proposed](https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-clear-site-data/issues/59 "External link (opens in new tab)") that this directive be removed from the specification for this reason, among others ([Firefox bug 1548034](https://bugzil.la/1548034 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

* `XMLHttpRequest` now outputs a warning to console if you perform a synchronous request while handling an [`unload`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/unload_event "unload"), [`beforeunload`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/beforeunload_event "beforeunload"), or [`pagehide`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/pagehide_event "pagehide") event ([Firefox bug 980902](https://bugzil.la/980902 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

* The Network monitor [request list](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/devtools-user/network_monitor/request_list/index.html#filtering-requests "External link (opens in new tab)") now allows you to block a specific URL ([Firefox bug 1151368](https://bugzil.la/1151368 "External link (opens in new tab)")).
* You can now resend a network request without editing the method, URL, parameters, and headers, using the [Resend](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/devtools-user/network_monitor/request_list/index.html#context-menu "External link (opens in new tab)") command on the context menu ([Firefox bug 1422014](https://bugzil.la/1422014 "External link (opens in new tab)")).
* The context menu of the Network monitor [Headers](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/devtools-user/network_monitor/request_details/index.html#headers "External link (opens in new tab)") tab now allows you to copy all or some of the header information to the clipboard in JSON format ([Firefox bug 1442249](https://bugzil.la/1442249 "External link (opens in new tab)")).

sources.content:
`getUserMedia()` is a powerful feature that can only be used in [secure contexts](/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts); in insecure contexts, `navigator.mediaDevices` is `undefined`, preventing access to `getUserMedia()`. A secure context is, in short, a page loaded using HTTPS or the `file:///` URL scheme, or a page loaded from `localhost`.

The `getUserMedia()` method is only available in [secure contexts](/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts). A secure context is one the browser is reasonably confident contains a document which was loaded securely, using HTTPS/TLS, and has limited exposure to insecure contexts. If a document isn't loaded in a secure context, the [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) property is `undefined`, making access to `getUserMedia()` impossible.

`NotAllowedError` [`DOMException`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/DOMException)
:   Thrown if one or more of the requested source devices cannot be used at this time. This will happen if the browsing context is insecure (that is, the page was loaded using HTTP rather than HTTPS). It also happens if the user has specified that the current browsing instance is not permitted access to the device, the user has denied access for the current session, or the user has denied all access to user media devices globally. On browsers that support managing media permissions with [Permissions Policy](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/Permissions_Policy), this error is returned if Permissions Policy is not configured to allow access to the input source(s).

Because of the obvious security concern associated with `getUserMedia()` if used unexpectedly or without security being carefully managed, it can only be used in secure contexts. There are a number of insecure ways to load a document that might, in turn, attempt to call `getUserMedia()`. The following are examples of situations in which `getUserMedia()` is not permitted to be called:

[`TypeError`](/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypeError)
:   Thrown if the list of constraints specified is empty, or has all constraints set to `false`. This can also happen if you try to call `getUserMedia()` in an insecure context, since [`navigator.mediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/mediaDevices) is `undefined` in an insecure context.

**Secure context:** This feature is available only in [secure contexts](/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts) (HTTPS), in some or all [supporting browsers](#browser_compatibility).

In addition, user permission is always required to access the user's audio and video inputs. Only a window's top-level document context for a valid origin can even request permission to use `getUserMedia()`, unless the top-level context expressly grants permission for a given

`SecurityError` [`DOMException`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/DOMException)
:   Thrown if user media support is disabled on the [`Document`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document) on which `getUserMedia()` was called. The mechanism by which user media support is enabled and disabled is left up to the individual user agent.

The **`getUserMedia()`** method of the [`MediaDevices`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices) interface prompts the user for permission to use a media input which produces a [`MediaStream`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaStream) with tracks containing the requested types of media.

As an API that may involve significant privacy concerns, `getUserMedia()`'s specification lays out a wide array of privacy and security requirements that browsers are obligated to meet.

Attempting to access `getUserMedia()` in this situation will result in a [`TypeError`](/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypeError).

